Requirement R01 (input): Input Autopilot Parameters. Fixed modalities: Touch and Keyboard. Intent: Allow the pilot to configure autopilot values (altitude, heading, speed) for engagement..

We will design this requirement in three sequential layers, all within THIS conversation: Function first, then Behaviour, then Structure. Conduct the sequence yourself — when a layer is agreed, state its final label clearly and move to the next.
- Functions: propose 2-3 genuinely distinct candidates labeled F-01.1, F-01.2, ... Distinct means each opens a different interaction goal — not the same goal reworded.
- Behaviours: one distinct interaction idea per fixed modality pathway (e.g. one Touch-only, one Keyboard-only), plus a Mixed pathway if it adds real value beyond the two. Labeled Be-01.<F>.1, Be-01.<F>.2, ... using the closed F index.
- Structures: 2-3 distinct sets of concrete HMI elements, labeled S-01.<F>.<Be>.1, ... using the closed F and Be indices.

Start with the Function candidates now (state the intent back first). The designer closes the whole requirement at the end.

**Intent restated:** Enable the pilot to set autopilot target values (altitude, heading, speed) so the autopilot can be engaged/executed with those parameters — using Touch and Keyboard.

**Function candidates:**

**F-01.1 — Parameter provision.** The HMI's purpose is to capture pilot-specified autopilot target values and make them available to the aircraft for engagement. Goal: the artefact exists to *convey desired flight-state targets* into the system.

**F-01.2 — Parameter validity assurance.** The HMI's purpose is to ensure the values that reach the autopilot are within valid/safe operational envelopes before commitment. Goal: the artefact exists to *guarantee the correctness/admissibility* of what gets set — a different teleology (protection against bad input) than mere provision.

**F-01.3 — Configuration-state legibility.** The HMI's purpose is to make the currently-set autopilot configuration knowable to the pilot at a glance. Goal: the artefact exists to *hold and expose the intended target state* so the pilot knows what is armed — distinct from entering it or validating it.

Note: F-01.3 is a strong candidate for **sharing** — the "expose current autopilot config" goal will likely recur in R covering autopilot engagement feedback (UC 1.2.7) and disengagement. Flagging now; don't design it exclusively here.

Which function do you want to close on? My lean is **F-01.1** — it's the core intent of an *input* requirement; validity (F-01.2) and legibility (F-01.3) are supporting functions better handled as their own requirements.
